title: A Faster Way to Find Hidden Pulsars in NASA Fermi Data
paragraphs: A pulsar is a very small, dead star that spins quickly and sends out a beam of light. Fermi, a NASA space telescope, has looked at the sky for 15 years. Its data is free for everyone, but many pulsars are still hidden in it.

Fermi catches only a few particles of light from each pulsar, and they are mixed with a lot of noise. To find a pulsar, scientists must guess three things at the same time: how fast it spins, how fast it slows down, and where it is in the sky.

A team led by Daniel Pook-Kolb in Germany found a clever way to do this. They treated the search like a puzzle in geometry. The method found a new pulsar that spins 261 times every second. The search took about 10 hours on a normal computer. The team says it is about a million times faster than older methods.

questions.q: What did the new method find?
questions.a: A new pulsar that spins 261 times every second.

questions.a: It is about a million times faster.
